**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, assignment).**

**What I found.** Section 10.3 (p0063) is a bare "successors and assigns" clause with no consent mechanics in either direction. Searching the full document confirmed:
- No "change of control" language anywhere, and no "deemed an assignment" trigger.
- Termination is notice-based (90 days, p0024) with a termination payment if the Company terminates (p0026) — no HDI exit or re-pricing right tied to our change of control, so the walk-away threshold is not hit.

**Why it deviates.** The clause omits the asymmetric allocation the playbook requires: it does not confirm our right to assign to an affiliate or M&A successor, and it leaves HDI free to assign the site development and hosting obligations — potentially to a competitor of ours.

**Redline (validated, preferred level).** Inserted a new paragraph after 10.3 giving the Company consent-free assignment to affiliates and merger/asset-sale successors, requiring our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) for any HDI assignment with a flat bar on assignment to our competitors, and confirming that a change of control of the Company is not an assignment and gives HDI no termination, suspension or re-pricing right. The comment flags the mutual notice-based fallback if HDI resists the asymmetry.
